description: The plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy and population frequency, displaying two accuracy measures: initial and final. The x-axis is labeled “o_pop frequency (x10^4)” with a linear scale ranging from 1 to 19, with tick marks at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The “Initial Accuracy” is represented by a green line with square markers connected by solid lines; it begins at approximately 0.31 when o_pop frequency is 1, decreases to a minimum of approximately 0.24 at o_pop frequency 5, rises to approximately 0.46 at o_pop frequency 7 and ends at approximately 0.34 when o_pop frequency is 19. Error bars are present at each data point. The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a blue dashed line with circle markers; it starts at approximately 0.73 when o_pop frequency is 1, decreases to approximately 0.56 at o_pop frequency 3, and then increases to a peak of approximately 0.85 at o_pop frequency 9 before ending at approximately 0.88 when o_pop frequency is 19. Error bars are present at each data point.
